Cohort or aggregate sensitivity analysis

Source: R/sensitivity.R
cohort_sensitivity.Rd

Run robust inference without re-estimating the cohort-period coefficients. Relative period one is the first treated period; zero is the last untreated period. Each reported confidence set has pointwise, rather than simultaneous, coverage. On unbalanced panels the balanced-design mapping is approximate.

Usage

cohort_sensitivity(
  fit,
  restriction = "SD",
  M,
  target = "att",
  framework = "cohort",
  method = NULL,
  full.path = NULL,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  parallel = FALSE,
  cores = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  control = list(),
  balanced = FALSE,
  cohort.paths = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

A fitted object returned by cohort_fit() or cohort_input().

restriction

Either "SD" (smoothness) or "RM" (relative magnitudes).

M

Nonnegative sensitivity bounds. SD bounds are in outcome units; RM bounds are dimensionless multiples of each cohort's pre-period benchmark.

target

"att", "dynamic", or "cohort-dynamic".

framework

"cohort" (default) or "aggregate".

method

"FLCI", "Conditional", or "C-LF". The default, NULL, is C-LF under both SD and RM, as the paper recommends. FLCI is available only under SD.

full.path

For SD, restrict pure pre-treatment curvature as well? The default, NULL, is TRUE for FLCI and FALSE (post-only) for Conditional and C-LF, so the default SD analysis is C-LF under the post-only restriction. Not applicable to RM.

conf.level

Pointwise confidence level in (0.5, 1), default 0.95.

parallel

Logical; run independent inference tasks in parallel?

cores

Number of workers. Defaults to detected logical cores minus one, with a minimum of one. Workers are capped by the number of independent target/bound tasks, or signed components for a single RM task.

seed

Optional integer seed. Fixed seeds give results independent of worker count and preserve the caller's random-number state.

control

Named list of numerical controls; see the section "Numerical controls" of vignette("detailed-guide", package = "CohortHonestDiD"). max.refinements is a nonnegative integer (default 3; 0 disables retries). Eligible unresolved searches double the regular grid intervals per retry. max.evaluations is the cumulative limit on distinct confidence-set point evaluations per target/bound, including endpoint probes, topology audits, and retries. Simulated least-favorable critical values are reused. For Conditional inference, max.expansions (default 6) caps bilateral domain doublings, including the two required adjacent-domain agreements. Values 0 or 1 return domain_stability_limit and no set. Refinement restarts the same domains at a finer mesh within the shared budget. For Conditional grid.radius > 8, grid.points specifies the reference density at radius 8: the effective initial count grows enough to keep the initial spacing no coarser than that reference. At grid.radius <= 8, grid.points remains the literal initial count. Larger ranges require more evaluations and may exhaust the unchanged cumulative budget.

balanced

Logical. If TRUE, the target and, under aggregate inference, the aggregated event study use only the relative periods observed for every cohort, the balanced window. Default FALSE. See the section "Balanced targets".

cohort.paths

Only with balanced = TRUE under cohort inference: "full" (used when NULL) restricts each cohort's whole path, and "window" restricts each cohort's path only inside the balanced window. Supplying it otherwise is an error.

Value

A cohort_sensitivity object containing intervals (one row per connected confidence-set component), estimates, settings, and detailed results. Empty sets and numerical failures have explicit status rows. With balanced = TRUE, see the section "Balanced targets" for the added settings and the aggregation element. For FLCI results, results[[k]]$weights holds the weights of the linear estimator; flci_weights tabulates them.

Details

The defaults follow the paper's recommendation: cohort inference with the C-LF procedure, under the post-only restriction for SD. Request the full-path FLCI with method = "FLCI". The FLCI needs the stronger full-path restriction and should be used with caution when some cohorts contain only a few units. Inference uses the covariance stored in fit; use cohort_fit(covariance = "CR2") for the bias-reduced CR2 covariance.

Conditional and C-LF procedures return success = FALSE, a warning, and missing confidence-set bounds when the target is deterministic or a required moment has zero or numerically degenerate variance. The status is unsupported_zero_variance or unsupported_moment_variance. Singular covariance alone does not trigger this limitation. FLCI supports its exact zero-covariance limit.

Search diagnostics include search.attempts (attempt, grid.points, new.evaluations, cumulative.evaluations, success, status), final.grid.points, refinements, and test.evaluations. The requested grid size remains in settings. Refinement preserves endpoint tolerances and all certification checks; exhaustion returns a warning and no set. C-LF searches use certified outer bounds from their own first-stage acceptance inequalities. Under SD, support.certified, support, and search.domain record these bounds and the searched domain. Finite-grid agreement does not certify exhaustive interior topology.

Conditional inference searches concentric finite domains centered at a primitive-trend contrast, with a normalization-invariant sampling scale. The initial radius adds the plugin radius and grid.radius times this scale. Wider domains retain the regular mesh spacing. Two successive adjacent-domain agreements are required in addition to endpoint checks. topology.audit = FALSE skips interior mesh checks only; mandatory domain and endpoint checks remain. The automatic endpoint tolerance still uses the conventional target standard error, separately from the search scale. Diagnostics include search.center, search.scale, search.scale.source, initial.domain, search.domain, requested.domain, domain.stable, domain.expansions, agreement.streak, and domain.history. search.domain records evaluated coordinates; it is empty before any evaluation. requested.domain records a range blocked by an allocation or evaluation limit. Print and summary methods report searched ranges. Bounded numerical search does not rule out components outside those ranges; support.certified, topology.certified, and inversion.exact remain FALSE for Conditional results. Limits return a warning and no set. With topology.audit = TRUE, an additional shifted finer grid checks the quarter and three-quarter points of registered regular cells, independently of inserted anchors. Disagreement uses the same bounded refinement policy. Finite range and mesh checks can still miss arbitrarily narrow interior components or gaps, as well as components outside the searched range. Density diagnostics are initial.grid.points, grid.density.adjusted, reference.domain.radius, and reference.grid.spacing. The reference radius adds the same plugin radius to eight times the search scale. Integer ceiling and any necessary upward rounding preserve an initial spacing upper bound, not exact lattice nesting across separate radius requests. Settings retain the requested count; histories and final.grid.points record the effective counts. Starting at a larger count does not consume a refinement. Reference fields are NA when no wider-range calculation is needed or reached.

Balanced targets

The balanced window runs from relative period L to S. S is the last post-treatment period and L the earliest pre-treatment period that every cohort in fit has. Both are read from the coefficient labels, so the window is also defined for unbalanced panels and for cohort_input objects. With balanced = TRUE the ATT averages the cells of periods 1 to S, each cohort weighted by its mass in every period, and dynamic and cohort-dynamic targets are reported for periods 1 to S only. Under aggregate inference the aggregated event study is formed on periods L to S, with the same cohort weights in every period (balanced aggregation). This removes the change in the cohorts averaged at each period, but it changes the estimand. It does not remove the change in the not-yet-treated comparison groups, which enters the imputation and CS-NYT biases through the bias map W, so balanced aggregate and cohort inference can still differ.

Under cohort inference cohort.paths sets the cohort paths that the restriction uses. "full" keeps every cohort's whole path, as without balanced. "window" uses each path only inside the window: coefficients after period S are dropped, the RM benchmark is a cohort's largest change between periods L and 0, and the full-path SD restriction bounds only the pre-treatment second differences inside the window. Pre-treatment coefficients before L are kept, because the bias map and the imputation normalization use them. Under the post-only SD restriction both choices give the same plug-in identified set; their confidence sets can differ slightly, for example through the simulated C-LF critical value. On a balanced panel, imputation and CS-NYT give the same balanced cohort inference under either choice, but in general not the same aggregate inference.

With balanced = TRUE, settings also contains balanced, cohort.paths (NA under aggregate inference) and window (lower = L, upper = S). Aggregate results also contain aggregation: the aggregation matrix (aggregation_matrix), the aggregated coefficients (betahat) and their covariance (Sigma), the aggregate normalization, coordinate_info, and the aggregate target weights (targets, one row per target).

Examples

data(minimum_wage)
# \donttest{
fit <- cohort_fit(Y ~ D, minimum_wage, index = c("id", "year"))
# Default: C-LF under the post-only SD restriction.
result <- cohort_sensitivity(fit, M = c(0, 0.01), seed = 1)
plot(result)

# Balanced aggregation on the relative periods observed for every cohort.
balanced <- cohort_sensitivity(fit, M = 0.01, framework = "aggregate",
                               balanced = TRUE, seed = 1)
balanced$settings$window
#> lower upper 
#>    -2     1 
# }
